name: MI-05
label: Likely R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a +13 GOP partisan lean
Incumbent Tim Walberg running with a large financial advantage
Democratic challenger raised only about $56,000 with no outside support
Prediction markets price Walberg around 92% to win
model.rationale: The district's solid Republican lean, Walberg's incumbency, and his overwhelming fundraising edge over a minimally funded challenger all point to a comfortable Republican win. Markets agree, pricing the Democrat at only about 7 percent.
model.watch: A major late Democratic outside spending push or a broad midterm wave against the incumbent party could narrow the margin, though a flip remains unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Tim Walberg seeks another term in a south-central Michigan district that leans about 13 points Republican at the presidential level. He enters the general election as a well-established incumbent with roughly $1 million on hand, while Democrat Christian Vukasovich has raised under $60,000 and shows no outside spending support. Minor-party and independent candidates are on the ballot but lack resources.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and market pricing, both of which favor Walberg decisively. The forecast expects a Republican margin in the mid-teens, with a Democratic upset possible only in an extreme wave scenario.
